newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia key share index continues decline.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia key share index continues decline.

text.p: The key Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index resumed its decline soon after markets opened as a huge Malaysian trade deficit for June and foreign exchange curbs affected sentiment, dealers said on Tuesday
At 0145 GMT, the Composite Index was down 1.06 percent to 968.22.
But, five minutes later, the index had recouped slightly due to technical resistance and was down 0.98 percent or 9.61 points at 968.95.
Dealers said Bank Negara's curbs on swap transactions by Malaysian banks announced on Sunday and a 2.8 billion ringgit deficit for June released on Monday were affecting sentiment.
"The fear is that with all these troubles, Bank Negara may push up interest rates," said a dealer with a local brokerage.
But, he said there was strong support for the index between 950 and 960. "It should rebound from there," he added.

Technology Resources Industries, which announced a 42 percent rise in its first half profits, was up 22 cents at 3.82 ringgit. Telekom, the most heavily weighted share on the index, was up five cents at 9.30 ringgit.
Most other index weighted blue-chip shares were down between 10 and 30 cents.
